Below is a small patch that stops Prism from grabbing a `#` in the middle of things like URLs as the start of a “command”. We simply require that the prompt‐character (`$` or `#`) be followed by whitespace before it will be tokenized as a shell command. This leaves your URLs intact, while still highlighting real shell prompts (which always have a space after the prompt):

What this does:

- Adds a lookahead `(?=\s)` right after `[$#]`, so Prism will no longer treat `#pre-1-0-9…` in a URL as a shell prompt.
- Real prompts like `$ echo hello` or `# apt-get update` still have a space after the prompt symbol and will continue to highlight correctly.
